chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Ali ibn Ri'ab from al-Hasan al-Attar from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

"When the pilgrim reaches Arafat before the rising of dawn, then turns back from Arafat and does not catch the people at Jamarat, and finds that they have already proceeded (to Mina), then he should stand for a short while at al-Mash'ar al-Haram and join the people at Mina, and there is no penalty upon him." And whoever misses standing at al-Mash'ar, his Hajj is not valid under any circumstance, as indicated by what has been narrated:

key_terms.أَفَاضُوا: They proceeded/moved forward (referring to the flow of pilgrims)
key_terms.الْمَشْعَرِ الْحَرَامِ: Al-Mash'ar al-Haram, the Sacred Mound (typically Mount Arafat's smaller counterpart or the Mound itself)
key_terms.جَمْعٍ: Jamarat, the area where the stoning ritual takes place
key_terms.عَرَفَاتٍ: Arafat, the plain where the main standing of Hajj occurs
key_terms.مِنًى: Mina, the tent city near Mecca

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a pilgrim leaves Arafat before dawn and misses Jamarat?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the ruling for a pilgrim who departs Arafat before dawn and misses the main gathering at Jamarat, requiring only a brief pause at al-Mash'ar al-Haram to maintain validity. It establishes al-Mash'ar as a fundamental pillar (Fard) of Hajj, distinguishing between a minor omission that incurs no penalty and a complete absence that invalidates the ritual. This ruling underscores the Shia emphasis on the precise timing and sequence of the stoning ritual as a core obligation.
